about: What each applied change was made to move. One entry per change: a number from a run's digest (crucible_review.py METRICS), its value before the change, and the value wanted. Each review measures the open entries on the runs made on or after `since` and sets status to met, not_met or dropped. Numbers only: nothing about any problem a run worked on.

expectations.change: the repair attempt runs alone first; the other attempts start only if it fails and stop once one survives
expectations.why: in the first v5.0 run 130 of 302 agents worked on further attempts and 18 on one that was kept

expectations.change: staging the attempts must not leave more parts without a surviving attempt
expectations.why: a guard: the saving must not come from giving up on parts

expectations.change: the estimate shown at approval counts the retries a plan usually needs
expectations.why: the first v5.0 run used 302 agents against an estimate of 185

expectations.change: budget is kept for the parts the plan marks essential, and they start first
expectations.why: the assembly and the end-to-end proof never started in the first v5.0 run

expectations.change: acceptance lists are closed sets; test strength beyond the list and causes outside the part never buy a round
expectations.why: the two parts that ran ten rounds each had a clause over an open set

expectations.change: only a material leftover keeps a repaired result from full acceptance
expectations.why: 0 of 18 parts ended fully accepted in the first v5.0 run

expectations.change: the planner sizes a part to one component so a solver's context stays within one session
expectations.why: 53 of 100 solvers carried more than 300K tokens; the engine has no cap, so this rests on the planning rule

expectations.change: every agent is told to work in few, large steps: one script for related tool calls where the host has a script tool (Code Mode), batched calls and filtered output otherwise
expectations.why: the first v5.0 run needed 68.9 model calls per agent and re-read 13.6 million cached tokens per agent; the target is a guess of a fifth fewer, to be corrected by the first measured run

expectations.change: sessions started with the launcher keep an agent's cache one hour instead of five minutes
expectations.why: in the first v5.0 run 318 calls came after a command of 5 to 30 minutes and wrote 85.0 of 149.9 million cached tokens a second time; holds only for runs started from a session with the one-hour setting (the digest's host block says which)

expectations.change: sessions started with the launcher let twelve agents work at once instead of the machine's default
expectations.why: the first v5.0 run sat at the cap of six agents for 78% of its time; the target is a guess, a plan with few parts side by side cannot reach it, and it holds only for runs started from a session with the higher cap (the digest's host block says which)

expectations.change: a solver may hand bulk reading, a wide search or a long test run to a helper session, counted and closed by scripts/crucible_helper.py
expectations.why: a helper that is stopped, fails or runs out of time costs tokens and hands back nothing; holds only for runs in which a solver started at least one. The effect helpers are meant to have, fewer solvers past 300K tokens of context, is the number of v5.1-part-size (53 of 100 solvers on the first v5.0 run)
